top_signals.title: Taiwan’s Political and Security Future
top_signals.summary:
Taiwan faces mounting questions about its ability to defend itself, a bitter fight over defense spending, and uncertainty about Washington’s commitment to its security. Michael Hunzeker (George Mason University), Amanda Hsiao (RAND), and Peter Mattis (Jamestown Foundation) join Ryan to examine whether Taiwan is preparing fast enough for a possible war, what’s holding up a major U.S. arms package, and whether warmer relations between Washington and Beijing could come at Taipei’s expense.
